claim: HAOS 18.5 is the latest OS release, published 2026-11-06; annotated tag points to commit fc301f55
Supervisor 2026.11.0 published 2026-11-06
HAOS is built with Buildroot via a BR2_EXTERNAL tree; Makefile builds one defconfig per board target (14 defconfigs in buildroot-external/configs)
generic-x86-64 HAOS 18.5 builds upstream Linux 6.18.58 with AppArmor, Docker Engine, RAUC (D-Bus, network) and an EROFS root (lz4hc/lzma)
Pi 5 HAOS kernel is the Raspberry Pi vendor fork pinned to a raspberrypi/linux commit tarball, not upstream
Default HAOS slot sizes: kernel 24M, system 256M, bootstate 8M, overlay 96M
GPT layout: hassos-kernel0/system0, kernel1/system1, bootstate, overlay, data (data takes the rest); boot partition is defined separately

RAUC system.conf: statusfile on /mnt/boot/rauc.db; slots kernel.0/rootfs.0 = A and kernel.1/rootfs.1 = B by partlabel; boot partition is a single non-A/B slot (allow-mounted); keyring /etc/rauc/keyring.pem; Pi 5 uses a custom tryboot backend
RAUC bundles use format=verity and carry compatible+version; install-check hook rejects a mismatched compatible with exit 10
rauc-hook install-check compares RAUC_MF_COMPATIBLE with RAUC_SYSTEM_COMPATIBLE and repairs a corrupted grubenv
rauc-hook slot-post-install for class boot calls an undefined post_install_boot function; unreachable because the manifest only registers the install hook for the boot image
Production images get rel-ca.pem as RAUC keyring; development images get dev-ca.pem (dev+release); a locally generated self-signed cert is appended if not chained to dev CA

Release RAUC signing cert and private key are GitHub Actions repository secrets (RAUC_CERTIFICATE, RAUC_PRIVATE_KEY); CI falls back to a public self-signed cert if missing and checks validity >=760 days ('the OS support window, with margin')

New HAOS PKI (ECDSA P-384 root valid 2026-06-09 to 2046-06-09) added in PR #4757 (merged 2026-06-09); old RSA-2048 HassOS root expires 2028-05-14 and the new release CA is cross-signed by the old root; keyrings no longer contain CRLs and cert validity shortened to 4 years
PR #5053 (merged 2026-10-12) signs a SHA256SUMS of all release images with cosign sign-blob via GitHub OIDC (Sigstore); says Supervisor and the version repo already use the same approach
GRUB boots a slot only if OK=1 and TRY<3, increments TRY each boot, and falls to a rescue-shell entry if no slot qualifies; each slot also has a manual rescue entry

Pi 5 tryboot backend gives a staged slot exactly one firmware tryboot attempt; arming relies on /run/systemd/reboot-param '0 tryboot' (volatile), so a plain reboot or power cut drops the attempt and marks the slot bad
Supervisor marks the booted RAUC slot GOOD in Core.start() before Core and apps start, and even when the system is flagged unhealthy
mark_healthy calls rauc.mark(GOOD,'booted') then mark(ACTIVE) unless an update is pending

OS update: Supervisor downloads .raucb over HTTPS from the OTA URL template, calls RAUC Install over D-Bus, then raises REBOOT_REQUIRED; it does not reboot itself; job requires HEALTHY, INTERNET, RUNNING and SUPERVISOR_UPDATED
Supervisor auto_update defaults to True and Supervisor updates itself at startup when a newer version exists on its channel
Version/channel info is fetched from https://version.home-assistant.io/{channel}.json
No runtime container-image signature verification found in Supervisor 2026.11.0: the only match for content_trust/cosign in Python code is an unused constant ATTR_CONTENT_TRUST
App model 'signed' property returns False ('Currently no signing support'); docs state signed is always false and image signing is not checked
App security rating 1-8 starts at 5; full_access or Docker API access forces rating 1; manager/admin roles, host network and host PID lower it

App manifest (config.yaml) schema requires name, version, slug, arch; optional ingress, host_network, privileged capabilities, apparmor (default true), full_access (default false), hassio_role, backup_pre
Apps run with Docker's default AppArmor profile unless apparmor:false (unconfined) or the app ships its own profile (apparmor=<slug>)
Supervisor container is created --privileged with AppArmor profile hassio-supervisor and the Docker and containerd sockets mounted rw
The hassio-supervisor AppArmor profile is downloaded at boot over HTTPS from version.home-assistant.io/apparmor.txt (no separate signature check in the script)
systemd hardware watchdog: RuntimeWatchdogSec=300 on /dev/watchdog
Supervisor backup = plain outer tar with backup.json plus one inner tar per component; inner tars encrypted only when a password is set
Supervisor writes SecureTar v3 only if Core >= 2026.3.0, else v2
SecureTar v3 derives keys with Argon2id (opslimit 8, memlimit 16 MiB) and encrypts with libsodium secretstream XChaCha20-Poly1305
SecureTar v1/v2 derive an AES-128 key from the password with 100 unsalted SHA-256 rounds (AES-CBC)
HA blog (2026-03-26): SecureTar v3 rolls out with 2026.4 on 2026-04-01, audited by Trail of Bits (3 findings, all resolved), audit paid by the Open Home Foundation; old backups remain readable
HA docs: backups encrypted by default; Recommended schedule backs up daily, keeps 3, stores locally and on HA Cloud; HA Cloud keeps only one backup; recommends a copy on another system and off-site
Supervisor app login delegates username/password checks to Core (POST api/hassio_auth) with a local cache used when Core is down
Supervisor API identifies callers by unix socket principal or a per-app Supervisor token, then applies role regexes (default/homeassistant/backup/manager/admin; admin = .*)
Core local auth hashes passwords with bcrypt (12 rounds, input truncated to 72 bytes)
Core MCP server can require an admin user per config entry (CONF_REQUIRE_ADMIN) and supports a read-only mode
HAOS CI smoke tests boot the image in QEMU, run an OS update and then switch boot slot with 'ha os boot-slot other'
Issue #4632: Pi 5/CM5 users report update slot always marked bad and falling back (Apr-Jun 2026); closed 2026-11-03
Issue #4845: Pi 5 18.0->18.1 update reboots into old version; maintainer says HAOS 18 needs recent Pi firmware for tryboot, fix is firmware update then power cycle
Issue #5031: HAOS 18.3 on x86 with Realtek r8169 boots but loses network; user restored by 'os boot-slot other'; closed as duplicate with a workaround
Issue #4785 (open): HAOS 18 on Pi 5 with NVMe HAT reports I/O errors and filesystem corruption; user reverted via the other boot slot
Supervisor issue #7034: large backups uploaded to OneDrive had an invalid outer tar/PAX size so restore could not find backup.json; maintainer says fixed in securetar 2026.10.0 (Supervisor 2026.10.2)

Open Home Foundation is a Swiss non-profit Stiftung that owns Home Assistant (transferred 2024), funded by commercial partner fees (Nabu Casa, Apollo Automation) and donations; Nabu Casa sells Home Assistant Cloud and official hardware
